sheet-1-3.description: This part of sheet 1 continues sheet 2 northward along Hamburg Avenue, the present Main Street, from Larue Street at the bottom edge to the heavy line under the Bungalow inset at the top. Hamburg Avenue runs up the left third of the sheet. West of it lie blocks 1 and 3, divided by a Private Road about 750 feet north of Larue Street; east of it lie blocks 2 and 4, cut back on the east by the heavy outline of the inset of the railroad depot district and by a line marked No Exposure. The blocks are residential and thinly built: one- and two-storey frame dwellings set back from the avenue with sheds, a stable, a bake house with an oven and an automobile house on the west side, and dwellings, a storage building and a coop on the east side. Water pipes of four inches are drawn along the avenue, with a hydrant near the south end, and the width of the avenue (45 feet) and of the Private Road (30 feet) is lettered. The Sanborn key (legend) and two north arrows are printed in the lower left corner of this part. The part is drawn at 50 feet to an inch but at a different angle from sheet 2, with Hamburg Avenue nearly upright on the page.
notes: Hamburg Avenue is now Main Street.
The Private Road west of Hamburg Avenue is on the line of today's Hudson Street.
Placed from two junctions on Main Street only (Larue and Hudson): a helmert fit, so rotation rests on the line between them.
The north arrows in this part point about 33 degrees left of the page vertical; the fit gives about 46 degrees, so the arrows are not a reliable guide here.

Scale 50 ft to an inch; title circle, key and copyright on this sheet. Five parts separated by heavy lines: part 1 Main and School Streets with Franklin Public School, Presbyterian church and Church of the Immaculate Conception (located 1/2 mile S.W. of P.O.); part 2 At Bungalow strip of ten dwellings (1/8 mile S. of P.O.); part 3 Hamburg Avenue (now Main Street) north of Larue Street, Private Road = Hudson Street; part 4 Washington and Main with the N.Y.S.&W. R.R. freight house and depot, Washington Hotel, jail (3/4 mile S.W. of P.O.); part 5 At Brick Row (1 mile S. of P.O.). Only parts 3 and 5 placed.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: Main and School Streets, Franklin Public School, churches and cemetery (1/2 mile S.W. of P.O.) (location not identified with confidence: hypotheses (bend of Main at High Street; Main / Church Street junction) tested against modern streets and parcels did not fit both the street pattern and the Wallkill River crossing; needs identification on the 1928 edition (franklin-1928 sheets 6 and 7) of the bend of Main with School, then hand-picked control).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: At Bungalow: row of ten dwellings on an unnamed street (1/8 mile S. of P.O.) (no named street or junction drawn; needs identification of the row and parcel-corner control).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: Washington and Main with the N.Y.S.&W. R.R. freight house and depot, Washington Hotel and jail (3/4 mile S.W. of P.O.) (no surviving junction identified; by the 1928 edition this is Church Street and Railroad Avenue by the N.Y.S.&W. passenger depot, and Railroad Avenue is not in OpenStreetMap; needs hand-picked control on Church Street near Cork Hill Road and Dixon Road, checked against franklin-1928 sheet 7).

sheet-1-5.description: This inset in the lower right corner of sheet 1 is headed At Brick Row, located 1 mile S. of P.O., and shows the company housing of Brick Row south of the centre of Franklin Furnace. Its main subject is a single row of twelve attached two-storey brick dwellings, numbered 1 to 12, drawn along the bottom of the inset and facing south onto a street that runs just beyond the edge of the sheet. Behind the row stand a line of paired frame sheds and a row of small privies, and further back the open ground of block 13. Streets marked Vacant (no buildings fronting them) bound the inset on the left, along the heavy dividing line, and on the right edge. In the upper part of the inset a few scattered frame outbuildings and a shed appear near the heavy line, and at the right edge a separate group of attached dwellings numbered 13 to 16 is cut by the sheet edge. A north arrow is drawn in the inset. The inset is drawn at 50 feet to an inch, the same scale as the rest of the sheet; the row of dwellings measures about 236 feet on the sheet, matching the south side of the modern Brick Row loop off Taylor Road.
notes: Brick Row survives as a street name: a short loop south of Taylor Road.
Placed from one hand-picked point (the middle of the street in front of the row) with the scale of sheet 2 and the inset's own orientation; low confidence, position good to perhaps 10 to 15 m.

sheet-2-1.description: The main part of sheet 2 covers the business centre of Franklin Furnace (today Franklin borough) along Hamburg Avenue, the present Main Street, from Larue Street south past Parker and Sussex Streets to the bottom of the sheet. Hamburg Avenue runs up the left half of the sheet; east of it Nestor Street runs parallel from Larue Street southward, and High Street crosses the lower right of the part diagonally from Parker Street to the bottom edge. Larue Street forms the top of the drawn blocks east of Hamburg Avenue, and a Private Road leaves Hamburg Avenue westward between blocks of dwellings north of the centre. The blocks along Hamburg Avenue hold frame stores and dwellings, Quinn's Hotel and the Snyder House Hotel on the east side north of Parker Street, a row of attached dwellings on Larue Street, and stores, a drug store, a jewelry store, a barber, a bowling alley, a wines and liquors store and a picture theatre near Sussex Street. The post office stands on the north side of Sussex Street near its junction with High Street. West of Hamburg Avenue at Parker Street lies the yard of the N.J. Zinc Co. with a railroad switch and coal pockets running in from the west. East of Nestor Street the blocks are thinly built, with scattered dwellings and outbuildings along a steep bank; the area east of High Street is shown as a separate inset of Railroad Avenue on the same sheet. The part is drawn at 50 feet to an inch, with water pipes marked in Hamburg Avenue and the street widths lettered at the corners.
notes: Hamburg Avenue is now Main Street.
Sussex (Street) is now Junction Street; the stretch west of Hamburg Avenue is unlabelled on the sheet.
The Private Road west of Hamburg Avenue near Larue is on the line of today's Mill Street.
Nestor south of about the middle of block 6 no longer exists; today's Nestor Street ends further north.
The post office stood on Sussex Street (Junction Street) at High Street in January 1911.
The High Street / Sussex junction was hand-picked: the detector does not find it beside the heavy line that bounds the Railroad Avenue inset.

Scale 50 ft to an inch. Three parts: part 1 downtown along Hamburg Avenue (now Main Street) with Larue, Nestor, Parker, Sussex (now Junction Street), High and a Private Road (now Mill Street), post office at Sussex and High; part 2 Railroad Avenue and the Wallkill River, block 11 (located 1/4 mile N.W. of P.O.); part 3 Railroad Avenue with the L.&H. R.R. and N.Y.S.&W. R.R. and the L.&H. station (1/2 mile N.W. of P.O.). Only part 1 placed.
